Uncomplicate. 
Innovate.
Imagine a world…where a cement manufacturer 
aims to reduce its carbon footprint and meet its sustainability targets with agility. A shipping company wants to cut down its operating costs substantially. An aviation company seeks to achieve always-on, anywhere-on connectivity for its crew.
None of these milestones would be possible 
for the enterprises, without the support of a strong digital foundation —one that underpins everything from cloud infrastructure and network operations to delivering exceptional customer experiences, powered by AI and Innovations. 
The global business landscape is undergoing 
a radical shift, with new challenges and opportunities emerging on the horizon. Delivering a seamless experience is not easy as enterprises face the challenges of integrating and managing a complex array of technologies, often with a mix of legacy tools and infrastructure. Moreover, data silos, fragmented systems and disparate processes make it difficult for them to deliver omnichannel, contextual interactions. Add to it the ever-increasing security and privacy concerns.At Tata Communications, our Digital Fabric aims 
to remove these roadblocks by offering a unified platform that simplifies management, enhances visibility and provides a secure foundation for building hyperconnected ecosystems.
Given the complexity around lack of omnichannel 
consistency, need to deploy solutions across technologies, privacy concerns etc., coupled with the customer's requirement to be future ready, our Digital Fabric provides Real-time, Always-on, Anywhere-on, Seamlessly Collaborative, Integrated Data Analytics and Intelligence, helping our customers stay ahead of the curve.
Our digital fabric brings together tools and 
expertise that can help businesses simplify large digital infrastructure, uncomplicate their IT estate and provide more visibility and control across various infrastructure systems including network, cloud and security. It facilitates the exchange of data, information and intelligence across diverse digital systems and applications.
By focusing on a strong digital foundation, 
global businesses can navigate headwinds and 
set the stage for future growth and innovation.Why Tata Communications? 08

About the Report
Our Integrated Annual Report adheres to the framework and guiding principles 
established by the International Integrated Reporting Council (‘IIRC’). It 
demonstrates our overall strategies and initiatives to the management of our 
business, creating value for our customers and other stakeholders.
Integrated Thinking in Action
We apply integrated thinking to shape our  
response to:
	 Material matters that affect our ability to create value
	 Short, medium and long-term priorities across financial 
and non-financial outcomes
	 Strategic resource allocation to strengthen 
competitive resilience
	 Sustainability imperatives including climate action, digital 
inclusion and human capital development
Our six capitals are integral to this process and determine 
 how we set targets, measure outcomes and manage trade-
offs. These capitals—financial, manufactured and intellectual, 
natural, human, social and relationship—are consistently 
referenced across this Report.
Our Reporting Framework
This Report is prepared in accordance with the guiding 
principles and content elements of the International 
Integrated Reporting Council ('IIRC') Framework, with 
disclosures mapped to the Global Reporting Initiative 
('GRI') Standards where applicable. Financial and statutory 
disclosures comply with the following:
	 The Companies Act, 2013
	 Indian Accounting Standards
	 SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015
	 Secretarial Standards issued by the Institute of Company 
Secretaries of IndiaForward-looking Statement

Reporting Period

to March 31, 2025). Where relevant, comparative data

contextual perspective.

and includes relevant information on our subsidiaries, 
associates, and key operating geographies where it is 
material to our performance and value-creation narrative. 
Any exclusions or boundary limitations are disclosed in the 
relevant sections.The sustainability content aligns with internationally 
recognised disclosure practices and reflects our 
environmental, social and governance ('ESG') priorities across 
operations. The sustainability KPIs are disclosed in detail on

Why Tata Communications?
Because evolved hyperconnected 
ecosystems is the future
From the convergence of media to 
AI powered customer engagement, 
from the rise of hybrid workplaces 
to the acceleration of borderless 
commerce, enterprises today 
demand scale, agility, intelligence 
and seamless integration. We 
stand at the confluence of these 
transformative shifts – driving 
strategic expansion, sustained 
growth and responsible operations.
Our strategy is shaped by this 
evolving enterprise landscape, where 
integration and intelligence are no 
longer optional but foundational. 
Guided by disciplined capital 
allocation, platform integration and 
a purpose-led approach to growth, 
we are executing with clarity and 
conviction. Our ambition to double 
data revenue is built around a 
multi-dimensional scale – expanding 
enterprise relevance while staying 
true to responsible business 
principles. We are strengthening 
digital infrastructure, accelerating 
the integration of acquisitions 
and capturing the full potential of 
cloud, AI and IoT.
With a future-ready Digital 
Fabric, deep domain expertise, 
and a trusted global presence, 
Tata Communications is the 
partner of choice for enterprises 
navigating the next frontier of 
digital transformation. Global leadership in digital 
infrastructure solutions
Acquisitions accelerate 
capability enhancements
Rising data revenue share, 
growing relevanceWe are providing seamless, high-speed 
and secure connectivity across the globe 
through our extensive network and agile 
digital infrastructure. We have the ability 
to connect cloud to cloud, data centre to 
cloud, user to cloud as well as within and 
across cloud in minutes, with a superior 
customer experience. A healthy order book, with a 
growing funnel
We have a healthy order book with a robust funnel driven 
by sectoral tailwinds and customer trust. New order 
wins are well-distributed across verticals, geographies 
and offerings. The increase in order book is owing to our 
continuous investment in portfolio expansion and capacity 
expansion of our sales division. This diversity, combined 
with long-term contracts and customer loyalty, provides 
stable revenue and sustainable growth.
Led by experience, 
built for scale
Leadership continuity has been vital in powering our 
transformation journey. Our management team brings 
domain expertise, execution focus and a shared vision 
for a sustained future. Powered by a proven track 
record of delivering on capital allocation, integration 
and profitable growth, the leadership team has 
consistently balanced ambition with a disciplined 
approach. The stewardship has been vital in reshaping 
our portfolio and instilling a performance-led culture.
Sustainable by design
We are building a digital future that is inclusive, 
responsible and climate-conscious. Our commitment to 
be Net Zero by 2035 is backed by measurable actions, 
including reductions in Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, 
increased use of renewable energy and investments 
in green infrastructure. ESG principles are embedded 
across our supply chain, governance practices and 
portfolio innovation. Our approach to sustainability is 
strategically aligned with customer expectations and 
long-term stakeholder value.Our recent acquisitions, which include 
The Switch and Kaleyra, have strategically 
expanded our reach and product 
offerings. The Switch enhanced our 
production capabilities and presence in 
North American media and entertainment 
market, while Kaleyra strengthened 
our Customer Interaction portfolio 
capabilities. These integrations aim 
to increase revenue and leverage 
our infrastructure.
Data drives 84% of our revenue, 
validating our transformation into a 
digital solutions provider. Our enterprise 
customers are investing in cloud, security, 
next-gen connectivity, Media and IoT 
solutions, which are cumulatively driving 
the expansion of our digital portfolio. The 
digital portfolio comprises 47% of our 
data revenue and is growing significantly 
(21.4% CAGR) since FY 19-20.

Letter from the Chairman
Dear Shareholders,
I feel immensely pleased and honoured to 
share my thoughts with you for the first 
time as the Chairman of the Board and 
present the Integrated Annual Report of Tata 
Communications for the financial year 2024-25. 
With an overarching objective to empower 
enterprises by connecting them seamlessly, 
protecting their digital ecosystems, and driving 
innovation through cutting edge technologies, 
your Company is committed to delivering 
advanced, integrated solutions that not only 
respond to today’s business demands but also 
anticipate the challenges of tomorrow. Your 
Company’s robust digital fabric combines 
infrastructure, platforms and services through 
an orchestration and management layer that 
enables enterprises to uncomplicate their 
digital infrastructure, transform their cost 
structure and unlock new growth avenues. 
We are well-positioned to drive digital 
transformation for enterprises with Innovation, 
AI, Automation and Sustainability built into 
our business model.
Performance
Operating in an increasingly unpredictable 
macro environment, your Company achieved 
consolidated revenue from operations 
of H23,109 crore for FY 24-25 and our 
profit margins were stable. The Board has 
accordingly proposed a dividend of H25 per 
share for FY 24-25 subject to the approval of 
the shareholders. Navigating Geopolitical Headwinds
Moderate global growth, changes in the geopolitical 
scenario, including tariffs worldwide and uncertainties 
surrounding sanctions, pose challenges. Your Company 
continues to navigate these challenges and remains 
resilient. While these tariffs may impact IT spending for 
our customers, the Company is confident in overcoming 
these obstacles through the value additions it has 
demonstrated to its customers across all its fabrics.
Future is Hyperconnected
Enterprises today need secure, flexible networks that 
can adapt to evolving business demands and ensure 
seamless user experiences. The shift to hybrid cloud, 
rising compliance needs, and the growth of AI, IoT, and 
edge technologies are accelerating demand for advanced 
cloud networking and digital transformation solutions. 
Tata Communications’ product and services portfolio 
delivers curated and effective solutions that address 
these client needs.
Your Company’s progress rests on strategic investments in 
technology, partnerships and sustainability.
On the technology front, Tata Communications is 
advancing next-generation technologies including its Cloud 
fabric, AI and IoT. For example, the newly launched Tata 
Communications Vayu, seamlessly integrates Infrastructure 
as a Service ('IaaS'), Platform as a Service ('PaaS'), AI 
Platform, Security, Cloud Connectivity and professional 
services into a single, intelligent ecosystem. 
For the 11th consecutive year, Tata Communications has 
been recognised as a leader in the 2024 Gartner® Magic 
Quadrant™ for Global WAN Services. Your Company’s 
growth strategy has been to successfully migrate 
customers to higher revenue bands, while maintaining 
execution brilliance. 
This effort is reflected in us being an Industry Leader with 
a Net Promoter Score ('NPS') of 82, indicating strong 
customer support and loyalty. 
Elevating our Sustainability Quotient
Our commitment to inclusive and sustainable growth 
extends beyond business. In line with Project Aalingana 
– the Tata Group’s unified commitment to a greener, 
more sustainable future – Tata Communications is proud 
to play its part through focused initiatives around skill 
development, community well-being, climate action, 
circular economy and water stewardship, integrating 
environmental responsibility into our core business 
strategy. Our CSR programmes promote digital literacy 
and STEM learning in underserved communities, while 
initiatives in employability and women empowerment are 
helping build resilient livelihoods. We are also stepping 
up our efforts in climate action and water conservation — 
through afforestation drives, watershed development and I believe that we are well-placed to 
lead in India and compete globally. Our 
focus on innovation, putting customers 
first and building a sustainable 
future will continue to shape our 
journey ahead. As we look forward, 
I am confident in our ability to drive 
meaningful impact and unlock long-
term value for all our stakeholders.sustainable water management programmes across high-
stress regions, like Nanneer Lake Restoration in Tamil Nadu. 
Internally, we are taking decisive steps to reduce our 
environmental impact and build a future-ready, responsible 
enterprise. Our pledge to achieve Net Zero by 2035 across 
our global operations remains a goal that anchors all our 
efforts. We are proactively mitigating climate change by 
reducing GHG intensity, with a consistent year-on-year 
decline in GHG emissions per million in revenue. Our 
investments in energy efficiency projects across offices 
and networking centres have already saved 9.8 million 
kWh of energy, enhancing operational sustainability. 
As we power digital progress, we remain equally 
committed to creating a more equitable, connected and 
sustainable world. Your Company has set an absolute 
emission reduction target validated by Science Based 
Targets initiative ('SBTi') and is executing operational 
improvements to achieve it.
Enabling AI
You Company has accelerated its vision through use of 
AI across its Network fabric, Cloud fabric and Customer 
Interaction Suite. The use of AI will help us optimise 
performance, enhance network monitoring and speed up 
our decision making, thereby increasing reliability and 
efficiencies across our solutions.
Leading the Way
The growing demand for digital services opens exciting 
opportunities for your Company. With strong positions in 
Network, Cloud & Security, Interaction, and IoT, I believe 
that we are well-placed to lead in India and compete 
globally. Our focus on innovation, putting customers first 
and building a sustainable future will continue to shape our 
journey ahead. As we look forward, I am confident in our 
ability to drive meaningful impact and unlock long-term 
value for all our stakeholders.
On behalf of the entire Board, I extend our heartfelt 
gratitude to Ms. Renuka Ramnath, who retired this year 
as our Chairperson and Independent Director, for her 
invaluable guidance and steadfast leadership over the past 
decade. Her contributions and leadership have left a lasting 
impact. As we look to the future, I am pleased to warmly 
welcome Ms. Sangeeta Anand, Mr. Sujit Kumar Varma and 
Mr. P. Jagdish Rao to the Board—we look forward to their 
insights and partnership on our journey ahead.
In closing, I extend my heartfelt gratitude for your 
continued support and trust in Tata Communications, 
as it accelerates its engine of innovation and 
sustainable growth. 
Regards,
N. Ganapathy Subramaniam
Chairman

Dear Shareholders,
It is my privilege to present Tata 
Communications’ Integrated Annual Report 
for the financial year 24-25. As we reflect 
on the year, I am proud of the progress 
we have made in delivering innovation, 
resilience and sustainable growth, despite 
global macroeconomic uncertainties and 
shifting global trade dynamics. As the 
world continues to redefine the boundaries 
of connectivity and intelligence, Tata 
Communications has moved forward with 
purpose, strengthening our position as the 
digital fabric of enterprises around the globe. 
Notwithstanding the operational headwinds 
and potential delays in enterprise decision-
making, our differentiated digital fabric 
continues to reinforce our relevance  
to customers positioning us well for  
FY 25-26 and beyond. Accelerating strategic transformation
In FY 24-25, we advanced our vision of enabling 
hyperconnected ecosystems with a sharp focus on 
financial fitness and deepening our capabilities in 
AI, cloud, cybersecurity, IoT and next-generation 
connectivity. Our commitment to driving value creation 
has been reflected in our financial performance. 
A key highlight of the year was robust growth in our 
digital portfolio revenue, maintaining strong momentum 
over the past two years. Our Enterprise revenue from 
both the domestic and international markets also 
saw good YoY growth. Our order book has grown 
significantly YoY, and is now well diversified, reflecting 
our successful transformation over time.
During the year, our consolidated revenue from 
operations reached H23,109 crore, reflecting a 11.2% 
year-on-year growth. Our data revenue, which 
forms the backbone of our business, grew by 13.7% 
YoY to H19,513 crore, while digital portfolio revenue 
surged by 29.5% YoY. 
Our strategic interventions, including the divestment of 
non-core assets such as Tata Communications Payment 
Solutions Limited, land parcel monetisation at Ambattur 
and enhanced subsidiary profitability, have strengthened 
our balance sheet and sharpened our focus on high-
growth areas. These efforts reduced our net debt-to-
EBITDA ratio to 2.06x, nearing our goal of below 2x.

Network Fabric
In FY 24-25, our Network Fabric, encompassing 
core and next-generation connectivity, delivered a 
robust performance. Driven by strong demand for 
data centre-to-data centre (DC-to-DC) connectivity, 
we achieved a steady year-on-year revenue growth 
of 3.2%. Our next-generation connectivity portfolio 
recorded an impressive 13.4% year-on-year growth, 
with our IZOTM Hybrid WAN and IZOTM Multi-Cloud 
Connect solutions driving large-scale network 
transformations. The latter achieved a revenue CAGR 
of over 50% over the past three years, securing 
strategic contracts across BFSI, automotive and 
airline sectors. Our transformation of the Tier 1 
network into a software-defined, AI-enabled platform 
with 99.8% first-time-right deployments and 95%+ 
proactive fault diagnosis has strengthened our global 
scale, delivering predictable performance and SLAs 
across 150 countries.
Interaction Fabric
The Interaction fabric, which includes collaboration 
and managed Communications Platform as a Service 
('CPaaS') solutions, experienced a 51.9% growth 
aided by inorganic investments. Throughout the year, 
we expanded our offerings to include programmable 
voice, video, Rich Communication Services 
('RCS'), and WhatsApp channels, while investing 
in channel and customer journey orchestration, 
boosting interaction intelligence through our 
Kaleyra.ai platform.
Cloud Fabric
The Cloud fabric delivered an impressive 10.5% year-
on-year revenue growth for the year, driven primarily 
by a major contract announced earlier in the year. 
Our security offerings have seen a strong order book, 
particularly in the BFSI sector.
IoT Fabric
Our IoT fabric, an incubation portfolio, achieved a 
remarkable 41.6% year-on-year revenue growth in  
FY 24-25. This was driven by the addition of new 
vehicles to our platform and a significant increase 
in data usage on our Tata Communications MOVETM 
platform. These developments are encouraging 
indicators of our strategy to drive platform 
growth in this segment.
Media and Entertainment Portfolio Success
The media portfolio recorded a 4.1% growth year-
on-year in FY 24-25. Our partnership with World Athletics was another defining moment for us last 
year. As part of this, Tata Communications will 
manage broadcast operations and production for all

Tata Communications  
Beacon Platform  
AI/ML is already transforming how enterprises orchestrate hybrid infrastructure and Tata 
Communications Beacon puts that power directly into the hands of operations teams. Instead 
of drowning in alarms and fragmented dashboards, Tata Communications Beacon uses pattern 
mining and AI-based correlation to surface the root cause. Built on the pillars of Discoverability, 
Manageability and Security, it enables Network Agnostic Fault and Performance Prediction 
across WAN, LAN and wireless environments.
 
The platform uses AI/ML based correlation of Network Alarms and uses Sequence Pattern 
Mining for detecting the zone of fault (overlay or underlay) or predicting the occurrence of fault 
in advance with greater prediction accuracy and higher coverage. Tata Communications Beacon 
does not just show what is happening, it can act on it too. The platform democratises AI through 
its ML Studio interface, enabling customers to accelerate their AI/ML maturity journey and 
advance towards cognitive network capabilities. With ML Studio interfaces, teams can visualise 
alarm clusters, predict degradation and trigger auto-resolution workflows without needing a 
data science background.

AI Driven Use-cases 
Our IoT fabric seamlessly integrates sensor data 
across multi-network environments through a

Offering a comprehensive solution that spans

time analytics and decision-making at the

helping businesses thrive in a fast-paced, 
data-driven world.

Our RoCE, EBITDA Margin and other KPIs have moderated due to certain management actions taken over the past

The new integrations, Kaleyra and Switch are nearing inflection points, with synergies expected to materialise in 
the coming quarters.
We also monetised land assets and divested from our payment solutions business and NetFoundryTM, enhancing 
profitability and reducing net debt. Continued debt reduction and profitability improvements are expected to 
support RoCE growth, with key metrics returning to target ranges as we are realising the synergies.

Cybersecurity Solutions-Achieving Cyber Resilience   
 
Our integrated cybersecurity portfolio—covering 
network, cloud and endpoint security, along with 
advanced threat intelligence—enables organisations 
to proactively manage evolving digital risks. Built 
on industry-leading frameworks like Zero Trust and 
MITRE ATT&CK®, our solutions deliver predictive threat 
detection, rapid incident response and enhanced 
regulatory compliance. Through Security Consulting and 
Managed Services, we have strengthened clients’ cyber 
resilience, safeguarding over 50,000 remote users and 
mitigating thousands of DDoS attacks. These intelligent, 
scalable solutions reinforce our role as a trusted partner 
in secure digital transformation.
Our Threat Intelligence Advisory Services provide 
customers with actionable insights into emerging risks, 
ransomware trends and threat actor behaviour, helping 
them stay ahead of cyber adversaries. We also support 
regulatory compliance and data privacy across sectors 
including BFSI, healthcare, and manufacturing. 
We have enhanced our DDoS (Distributed Denial-of-
Service) protection offering through AI-driven threat 
detection and response. We protected over 12,000 
customer profiles from DDoS attacks globally, mitigating 
more than 7,000 such attacks. This adaptive learning 
continuously refines threat signatures, minimising false 
positives and responding to evolving attack patterns. AI-
powered traffic behaviour analysis identifies anomalies in 
volumes, patterns and request frequencies, automating 
signature generation and deployment. This automation 
blocks malicious traffic within 60 seconds and improves 
incident response times.
Our disaster recovery automation service ensures 
business continuity by detecting failures, triggering 
failover workflows and enabling single-click recovery. What is shaping 
the future of 
the Cloud Market? Hybrid Cloud Recovery Time Objectives are reduced from hours to 
minutes, while automated reporting of disaster recovery 
drills and compliance enhances operational resilience. 
Tata Communications remains committed to 
empowering businesses with the tools and intelligence 
needed to navigate today’s complex cyber landscape—
ensuring operational continuity, customer trust and long-
term digital resilience.
As digital ecosystems continue to evolve, we

With a firm commitment to innovation, we aim

Ensuring business continuity through  
Managed Cloud services
Pitti Engineering Limited is one of India’s largest 
manufacturers of electrical steel laminations and 
precision machine components. They cater to diverse 
sectors with strong domestic and international presence.
Business challenge
Frequent outages disrupted ERP operations, affecting 
core functions such as demand planning and warehouse 
management. Ageing on-premise infrastructure led to 
downtime, revenue risks and operational inefficiencies. 
Managing the outdated data centre consumed 
significant IT resources. 
Our impactful solution
To ensure business continuity, we migrated Pitti 
Engineering’s critical SAP workloads to a robust 
AWS cloud environment. The managed public cloud 
service for AWS offered:
 Increased availability for critical workloads

to boost productivity while achieving meaningful

communication within India. These offerings come fully 
integrated with fixed-line and internet telephony services, 
including calling licenses, certified devices, seamless 
migration, and full-stack managed services.
 
Advanced Voice and Communication Solutions
We continue to enhance our enterprise voice portfolio, 
focusing on intelligent, customer-centric solutions. 
Our advanced call routing engine supports time-
based rules, percentage-based traffic distribution, 
and Global Emergency Reroute, ensuring operational 
resilience and uninterrupted connectivity. These 
capabilities are further augmented by features such 
as IVR, secure call recording, sentiment analysis, real-
time performance monitoring, and customer feedback tools. Additionally, we have simplified the customer 
journey by enabling self-service ordering and API-
based number procurement, empowering businesses 
to manage communication needs directly within 
their own ecosystems.

5Enhancing Workplace Safety with SafePassTM
The Dolvi plant of JSW Steel Limited, spanning 1,400 
acres, required a comprehensive safety solution to monitor 
worker movement, prevent safety incidents and ensure swift 
emergency response. To fulfil this objective, we implemented 
SafePassTM in the coke oven department, equipping workers 
with our IoT-enabled safety device to improve visibility, 
security and efficiency. This comprehensive solution 
offered real-time visibility of the movement and safety of 
each employee in each work zone, with the ability to react 
instantly to any anomaly or incident.

Our succession strategy focuses on proactive planning and future-readiness to ensure smooth leadership transitions 
and sustained growth.
A talent mapping exercise is in place to ensure a ready pipeline of incumbents for key leadership roles. This also 
involves establishing talent profiles on the capabilities, areas of improvement and growth trajectory followed by 
development interventions to be role ready.
Creating a future-ready workforce

Development Journey’ prepares employees for their aspired roles by building relevant skills and knowledge, while

learning paths, combining online courses and knowledge checks to ensure employees are equipped for future 
roles and challenges.Fostering a Culture That Inspires

Tata Communications is firmly committed to respecting 
and promoting human rights across its operations and 
value chain. Our Business & Human Rights (‘BHR’) Policy, 
approved by the MD and CEO and available on our 
website, addresses key issues such as anti-discrimination, 
fair wages, digital rights and modern slavery, aligned 
with internal policies and processes. The CSR, Safety and 
Sustainability Committee exercises oversight over the 
BHR Policy and was apprised of the BHR gap assessment 
findings and the related action plan during FY 24-25.
We uphold zero tolerance for malpractice and human 
rights violations. A comprehensive grievance mechanism—
including a robust Whistleblower Policy and independent 
Ethics Helpline—enables confidential, retaliation-free 
reporting by employees and stakeholders. No significant 
human rights grievances were reported during FY 24-25.
Integrating Human Rights across our operations 
We have embedded human rights into supplier 
engagement through our Supplier Code of Conduct, which 
forms an integral part of business agreements. A revised 
ESG Due Diligence Checklist — (for suppliers crossing 
an identified value threshold) ensures alignment with 
expectations on labour rights, ethics and sustainability. In FY 24-25, ESG assessments, conducted in partnership 
with EcoVadis, covered 55% of our key suppliers, enabling 
targeted improvement plans.
We also expanded our Supplier Diversity Programme, 
onboarding four new suppliers from underrepresented 
communities and launching a Diversity Questionnaire 
and awareness workshops to build their capabilities and 
inclusion in our sourcing ecosystem.
In FY 24-25, we began annual UNGC Communication on 
Progress submissions, reinforcing our commitment to 
its Ten Principles. We also updated our Modern Slavery 
Statement in line with the UK Act, affirming zero cases for 
forced, child labour and trafficking this year. In FY 24-25, 
98% of our employees completed the mandatory trainings 
on the Tata Code of Conduct and Dignity in the Workplace 
Policy which incorporate BHR principles. Two targeted 
sessions were also held for suppliers on responsible 
business practices and grievance mechanisms.
These efforts reflect our ongoing commitment to fostering 
a safe, ethical and inclusive workplace that upholds human 
rights at every level.

For Jayanti Devi from Periyardha village, life took an 
unexpected and devastating turn when her husband 
passed away. His prolonged illness had drained all their 
savings, leaving Jayanti with the heavy responsibility 
of raising five children on her own. In 2016, hope 
arrived when Project MPowered's team conducted 
a participatory rural appraisal with the community 
members in the village to identify vulnerable families 
for inclusion in the project, supported by Tata 
Communications and implemented by Trickle Up 
India Foundation. Through the project, Jayanti was 
introduced to the concept of Self-Help Groups. She 
joined a group, opened her first bank account and 
started saving regularly. She also received training 
in livestock management and sustainable farming 
practices from Smart Sakhis and the field staff. With 
financial aid from the project, she bought a goat and 
began cultivating vegetables on her small piece of 
land. Determined to build a stable future, she secured 
a loan from her SHG, expanded her vegetable farming 
and started selling her produce in the local market 
even attending up to three haats (local markets) 
per week. Her goat-rearing business also flourished, 
adding another source of income. Technology 
also became a game-changer for her. Through the 
project, Jayanti received a smartphone-a tool she 
initially found intimidating but soon mastered. Now, 
she uses it to access farming tutorials on the PoP 
(Package of Practices) App to further improve her 
agricultural techniques.Jayanti Devi  
Farmer turned Entrepreneur 
"I thought I wouldn't be able to do it-but I did. 
Today, I am not only providing for my family, but

my community." - Jayanti DeviJayanti's success story does not end just with

of how collective strength and empowerment can 
drive sustainable change.

Bringing Light, Changing Lives: Solar Power 
Transforms Chasikgindam
In the quiet village of Chasikgindam, a quiet revolution 
is underway—one powered not by grand gestures, 
but by sunlight. For Banio Sangma and his family, 
the shift has been nothing short of life-changing. Six 
years ago, Banio moved to Waru Songital with his 
family dreaming of a peaceful life. But that dream 
was dimmed—literally—by the absence of electricity. 
Like many others in the village, the Sangmas relied 
heavily on kerosene and candles, spending a large 
chunk of their income on temporary light. Many nights 
were spent huddled around a bonfire, and some 
dinners passed in darkness, stealing away the warmth 
of shared moments.
That changed through the Climate Resilient Village 
Programme, when Banio’s household received a solar 
energy kit setup. A seemingly simple setup, yet it 
brought profound change. The benefits go beyond 
lighting. Evenings, once constrained by darkness, are 
now filled with quiet joy—reading books, completing 
chores and savoring the comfort of a well-lit home. 
Freed from the financial burden of kerosene, the 
family can now redirect their resources toward other 
essentials, building a brighter and more secure future."Now, our lives are very different from before” 
-  Banio

Driving Change for Girls’ Hygiene and Safety
During his community immersion at the Government 
School in Kherli, Dausa, Anmol Chokhandre, a Gandhi 
Fellow trained under Project ANEW, identified a 
deeply concerning issue, i.e., the school’s toilet was 
in complete disrepair. This left all 52 enrolled girls 
without access to safe, hygienic restroom facilities. 
With no other option, the girls were forced to use 
nearby grasslands, exposing them to serious health 
risks, safety concerns and a loss of dignity. 
Recognising the urgency of the situation, Anmol 
collaborated with community members and 
emphasised how inadequate sanitation on the health, safety and academic performance of girl students. 
Empowered by the platform and encouraged by 
community support, the girls collectively demanded 
the repair and construction of a safe, functional 
toilet within the school premises. Their advocacy 
turned into action. 
As a result, the issue was prioritised and steps were 
swiftly taken to renovate and rebuild the toilets. 
This success story is a testament to the power of 
collaboration between communities, students and 
local leadership in creating meaningful, sustainable 
change in girls’ education and well-being.Nanneer LakeSchools in Action for the Planet

and social systems.
Our programme design takes into account regional 
disparities, particularly within Marginalised Women,

due to gender but also entrenched caste hierarchies. 
We prioritise interventions that apply our core strength—
digital solutions—to bridge systemic gaps. By integrating 
technology into skill development and livelihood The

We have moved beyond supplier compliance to supplier 
capacity building. Our Supply Chain Climate Action 
Framework addresses the emissions profile of our 
upstream partners. It is designed to integrate climate 
performance into procurement governance while 
establishing our role to influence and engage with 
suppliers in transforming our supply chain. Under this 
framework, we aim to work with responsible suppliers 
and contribute positively to our climate action goal of 
Net Zero by 2035. The intended result of this framework 
is for our suppliers to complete their GHG inventory, 
respond to CDP and formulate science-based emission 
reduction targets.
Environmental KPIs represent a part of our Supplier Code 
of Conduct, with clear mandates for suppliers to disclose 
emissions through CDP disclosure, commitment to 
science-based targets and build GHG inventories that act 
as reference points for emission reduction roadmaps.

Community-based Carbon Offset Initiatives
We approach offsetting through initiatives that 
deliver community-level impact. Our Smart 
Cookstoves Programme, registered under 
Verra’s Verified Carbon Standard, has helped cut

Odisha and Meghalaya. Total beneficiaries are

By reducing biomass dependence, the programme

household health. The resulting carbon credits

voluntary offset markets.

carbon neutrality strategy.

Water Stewardship
Tata Communications recognises water as a vital, 
limited, and shared resource, and is firmly committed 
to its sustainable management across all operations. As 
part of our environmental stewardship, we implement 
comprehensive measures to optimise water usage, 
including effective recycling, reuse practices and 
stringent leakage control at all major facilities. Regular 
internal audits are conducted to assess and enhance 
operational efficiency, while targeted training programs 
and awareness initiatives are carried out to engage 
stakeholders on the importance of responsible water 
use and conservation. Our strategic interventions such 
as wastewater recycling, deployment of rainwater 
harvesting systems and adoption of innovative 
technologies like IoT-enabled water meters, have 
significantly reduced our overall water consumption. 
We remain focused on continuously identifying and 
leveraging advanced solutions to further improve 
water efficiency and ensure long-term sustainability 
across our facilities.
Recycled water usage increased 
from 16% to  21%
Deployment of rainwater harvesting 
structures at high-consumption sites

Waste Management and Circular Economy
We treat waste not as a byproduct, but as a resource. 
From cafeteria composting to e-waste recycling, we 
have established clear systems to divert material from 
landfills and close the loop wherever possible. The 
entire waste generated is classified into 12 distinct 
categories to enable specialised treatment and 
material recovery. Organic Waste Converters installed 
at large facilities convert food and garden waste into 
nutrient-rich compost used for landscaping. To ensure 
traceability, waste handling is tracked through our 
internal Management Information Systems and disposal 
certificates are recorded and verified.
Non-hazardous wastes are handed over for recycling 
and other recovery options (waste to energy). In  
FY 24-25, we have been able to recycle 89%  of 
the waste generated in our facilities, which further 
strengthens our Zero Waste to Landfill by 2027 goal.
100%   
of our hazardous waste is recycledOur Water Stewardship Initiatives for Communities
At Tata Communications, our dedication to water

Chennai, Tamil Nadu: 
Since 2022, we have partnered with local

the lake’s water holding capacity and groundwater 
recharge. Additionally, the project has revitalised 
local biodiversity and transformed the lake into a 
vibrant community space, welcoming families for

flourish together.
Dharashiv, Maharashtra: 
We are working with local partners on integrated 
watershed development to restore canals and ponds 
and construct check dams. These interventions are 
improving water retention, raising ground water levels 
and enhancing soil fertility thereby ensuring reliable 
irrigation and supporting sustainable agriculture and 
rural livelihoods.
Through these projects, Tata Communications is 
not only working towards water neutrality but also 
fostering stronger, more resilient communities—
proving that with collaboration and care, sustainable 
water management can lead to flourishing ecosystems 
and brighter futures.

framework that inspires us to conduct ourselves 
with the highest standards of integrity and drive our 
business ethically. The TCOC defines the core values 
and principles that guide our business practices. To 
ensure that its principles are understood all employees

by regular policy-specific training sessions led by 
our Legal Compliance team. Our third-party partners 
engage with the TCOC through structured onboarding,

relating to business mentioned under Item Nos. 5 to 8 of the accompanying Notice.
In respect of Item No. 5
As per the provisions of Section 204 of the Act and Regulation 
24A of the SEBI Listing Regulations, the Company is required 
to undertake Secretarial Audit by a Secretarial Auditor who 
shall be a Peer Reviewed Company Secretary. Regulation 24A 
of the SEBI Listing Regulations, as amended, further requires 
the Company to obtain the approval of its Members for 
appointment or re-appointment of the Secretarial Auditors.
The Board of Directors of the Company (‘Board’) at its 
meeting held on April 22, 2025 appointed M/s. Parikh & 
Associates, Peer Reviewed Firm of Company Secretaries 
in Practice (Firm Registration No. P1988MH009800 / Peer 
Review No. 6556/2025), as the Secretarial Auditor of the 
Company for a term of five consecutive years, commencing 
from financial year 2025-26 till financial year 2029-30, 
subject to approval of the Members. If appointed, M/s. Parikh 
& Associates will carry out Secretarial Audit for financial 
years 2025-26 to 2029-30. M/s. Parikh & Associates have 
submitted their eligibility certificate and consent to act as the 
Secretarial Auditor of the Company and have confirmed that 
their proposed appointment, if made, will be in accordance with the conditions prescribed under Regulation 24A (1A) of 
the SEBI Listing Regulations.
The fee proposed to be paid to M/s. Parikh & Associates 
towards Secretarial Audit for FY 2025-26 shall be H2.50 lakhs 
per annuam (with an increase of 10% after every 2 years), 
excluding applicable taxes and out of pocket expenses, with 
the authority to the Board to make revisions as it may deem 
fit. There is no material change in the proposed fee payable 
to M/s. Parikh & Associates compared to that of the previous 
Secretarial Auditor. 
The fee for services in the nature of statutory certifications 
and other permissible non-audit services will be in addition to 
the secretarial audit fee as above, and will be decided by the 
Management in consultation with the Secretarial Auditors. 
The provision of such permissible non-audit services will be 
reviewed and approved by the Board.
M/s. Parikh & Associates is a well-known firm of Practising 
Company Secretaries founded in 1987 and based in Mumbai. 
Renowned for its commitment to quality and precision, 
the firm has been Peer Reviewed and Quality Reviewed by 
the Institute of Company Secretaries of India, ensuring the

Brief profile of Mr. P. Jagdish Rao:
Mr. P. Jagdish Rao, aged 65 years, is a seasoned financial 
services and technology executive with over 35 years of 
experience at Citibank and Citigroup, where he played a 
pivotal role in driving large-scale business transformations, 
optimising global banking operations, and implementing 
advanced technology platforms. He has deep expertise in 
cyber security, data analytics and corporate governance, 
having interacted extensively with the Citigroup Board for 
20 years. In his leadership roles, he managed technology 
infrastructure, corporate realty services and business 
operations worldwide. Mr. Rao spearheaded several strategic 
transformation initiatives such as consolidating Citi’s global 
data centers, cutting IT costs by over US$2 billion and 
implementing Citi’s Private Cloud infrastructure, which helped 
enhance digital and mobile banking capabilities. He also led 
the consolidation of Citigroup’s global real estate footprint, 
reducing it by over 60%, resulting in significant cost savings.
Throughout his career, Mr. Rao has held various senior 
leadership positions, including Chairman of Citigroup 
Technology Inc., Chief Administrative Officer for the Global 
Consumer Bank and twice serving as Citigroup’s Chief 
Information Security Officer (CISO). He has extensive 
experience in mergers and acquisitions, divesting several 
Citi subsidiaries globally and managing corporate operations 
across diverse regions such as Asia, Europe, Latin America 
and the U.S. His earlier career included roles in corporate 
banking, treasury and trade services, and transaction 
banking. With a strong educational foundation in engineering 
and business, Mr. Rao is recognised for his ability to lead 
and implement large-scale global transformations that align 
technology with business goals.
Mr. Rao is a graduate engineer in Electronics & Electrical 
Communication Engineering from the Indian Institute of 
Technology Kharagpur (1981) and has an MBA from the Indian 
Institute of Management Ahmedabad (1984). He has also 
completed the Advanced Management Program at Kellogg 
Business School, North Western University, Evanston, IL.

Company’s Performance
FY 2024-25 was a year of steady and sustained growth for Tata Communications, against the backdrop of ongoing global 
macroeconomic challenges. The Company continued to build momentum in the digital portfolio, which recorded a 29.5% year-
on-year growth and now constitutes nearly half of the overall revenues. This performance emphasises the growing relevance of 
our digital fabric strategy encompassing Network, Cloud, IoT, and Interaction fabrics. The order book and deal pipeline remain 
healthy, supported by large, multi-fabric wins across diverse geographies and industry verticals.
During the year, the Company took several strategic initiatives, including the monetisation of a large land parcel at Ambattur, 
Chennai and divestment of non-core subsidiaries such as Tata Communications Payment Solutions Limited. We have sharpened 
capital allocation and positioned the Company to prioritise investment in core business areas.As we enter FY 2025-26, Tata Communications is well-
positioned with a sharpened strategic focus, continued 
digital growth, and a roadmap for delivering sustainable, 
long-term value.
On a standalone basis, the revenue from operations for 
FY 2024-25 was H7,277.86 crore, lower by 8.93% over the 
previous year’s revenue of H7,991.68 crore. The profit after 
tax (‘PAT’) attributable to shareholders for FY 2024-25 was 
H1,050.87 crore as compared to PAT of H638.63 crore for the 
previous year. These changes reflect the impact of the hive-
off of the Company’s new-edged digital services business 
to Novamesh Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the 
Company at the start of the financial year. The increase in 
PAT is additionally attributable to the exceptional income 
from land monetisation during the year.
On a consolidated basis, the revenue from operations for FY 
2024-25 was H 23,108.59 crore, higher by 11.18% over the previous 
year’s revenue of H20,784.68 crore. The PAT attributable to 
shareholders and non-controlling interests for FY 2024-25 
was H1,836.78 crore as compared to H 969.58 crore for the 
previous year. The growth in consolidated revenue is driven by 
additional revenue and synergies from the entities acquired 
during the previous financial year, gain on land monetisation 
and strategic divestment of Tata Communications Payment 
Solutions Limited by the Company during the year.
Dividend
The Board recommends a dividend of H 25/- per fully paid equity 
share on 285,000,000 equity shares of face value H 10/- each, 
for the financial year ended March 31, 2025. The Board has 
recommended dividend based on the parameters laid down 
in the Dividend Distribution Policy, which can be accessed at  
www.tatacommunications.com/resource/corporate-
resources/policies/tcl-dividend-distribution-policy/.
The dividend on equity shares is subject to approval of the 
Members at the Annual General Meeting (‘AGM’) scheduled 
to be held on Wednesday, July 9, 2025.
The dividend, once approved by the Members, will be paid, 
subject to deduction of tax at source, on or after Thursday, 
July 10, 2025. If approved, the dividend will result in a cash 
outflow of H712.5 crore. The dividend on equity shares is 
250% of the paid-up value of each share. The total dividend 
pay-out works out to 38.79% of the consolidated profit after 
tax attributable to shareholders and non-controlling interest 
for FY 2024-25.
The Company has fixed Thursday, June 19, 2025 as the ‘Record 
Date’ and will close the Register of Members from Friday, 
June 20, 2025 till Monday, June 23, 2025 (both days 
inclusive) for determining entitlement of Members to final 
dividend for the financial year ended March 31, 2025, if 
approved at the AGM.

As on March 31, 2025, the authorised share capital of the

the Company has not issued any shares, securities /

Restructuring and Acquisitions
External Restructuring:
Pursuant to a Share Purchase Agreement (‘SPA’) dated 
November 13, 2024, the Company sold its entire stake in its 
wholly-owned subsidiary Tata Communications Payment 
Solutions Limited (‘TCPSL’) to Transaction Solutions 
International (India) Private Limited. Upon completion of all 
conditions precedent to the transactions stipulated under 
the SPA and receipt of a no-objection certificate from 
Reserve Bank of India, TCPSL ceased to be a wholly-owned 
subsidiary of the Company effective February 28, 2025.
Internal Restructuring:
During FY 2024-25, your Company has undertaken various 
internal restructuring activities for simplifying its existing 
layered group structure of subsidiaries, as follows:
1. The Company completed the transfer of its identified 
new-edged digital services business as a going concern 
to its wholly-owned subsidiary, Novamesh Limited, 
effective April 1, 2024.
2. Tata Communications MOVE B.V. and Tata 
Communications MOVE Nederland B.V., wholly-
owned indirect subsidiaries of the Company ceased 
to exist effective June 1, 2024 on account of their 
merger with their immediate parent company i.e., Tata 
Communications (Netherlands) B.V., also a wholly-
owned subsidiary of the Company.
3. The entire shareholding of Campaign Registry Inc., 
an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary incorporated 
in US was transferred from Buc Mobile Inc., to Tata 
Communications (Netherlands) B.V., both wholly-
owned subsidiaries of the Company, with effect from 
August 1, 2024.
4. Subsequent to the fresh issuance of 10,41,088 ordinary 
shares to the Company followed by the cancellation 
of the entire existing share capital issued to Tata 
Communications International Pte. Limited (‘TCIPL’), 
an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, 
Tata Communications (UK) Limited became a direct 
wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company effective 
September 27, 2024.
5. On December 20, 2024, Tata Communications Middle 
East Technology Services LLC (‘TC METS’) acquired 
99.5% shareholding of Solutions Infini FZ-LLC (‘SI UAE’) 
through a capital infusion. Thereafter, SI UAE transferred 
its entire business to TC METS vide an Intra-Group 
Business Transfer Agreement effective January 1, 2025.
6. Kaleyra UK Limited, transferred its entire business 
to Tata Communications (UK) Limited through an 
Intra-Group Business Transfer Agreement effective 
February 1, 2025.
7. Through an Asset Transfer Agreement, the entire 
assets and assumed liabilities of Buc Mobile, Inc. 
were transferred to Kaleyra US Inc. with effect from 
February 1, 2025.8. Pursuant to an Agreement dated January 30, 2025, 
the entire stake of Kaleyra Dominicana S.R.L. was 
transferred from Kaleyra US Inc. to Tata Communications 
(Netherlands) B.V. On completion of the transaction, 
Kaleyra Dominicana S.R.L. became a wholly-owned 
subsidiary of Tata Communications (Netherlands) B.V. 
from February 1, 2025.
9. Pursuant to the investment made by the Company in Tata 
Communications (Netherlands) B.V. (‘TC Netherlands’) 
and subsequent buy back of its existing share capital, 
TC Netherlands has become a direct wholly-owned 
subsidiary of the Company effective April 4, 2025.
10. Tata Communications SVCS Pte. Ltd., through an Intra-
Group Business Transfer Agreement dated March 31, 
2025 transferred its entire business to another step-
down subsidiary of the Company, viz., TC Networks 
Switzerland SA effective April 1, 2025.
11. Tata Communications (Hong Kong) Limited, a step down 
wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, incorporated 
TC (Shanghai) Network Services Company Limited 
in People’s Republic of China as its wholly-owned 
subsidiary with effect from April 18, 2025.

Details pertaining to energy conservation initiatives of Tata Communications are as follows:
Steps taken or impact 
on conservation of 
energyIn FY 2024-25, 169 energy-saving opportunities were implemented including projects on Heating, 
Ventilation and Air Conditioning (‘HVAC’), Switched-Mode Power Supply (‘SMPS’) and Uninterruptible 
Power Supply (‘UPS’) efficiency enhancement / Optimisation and Consolidation, Smart Lighting 
(conversion of conventional lighting into LED), and PUE enhancement. These projects resulted in 
energy savings of 9.8 million kWh (cumulative) and energy cost savings of H10.1 crore.
Steps taken by the 
company for utilising 
alternate sources of 
energyTata Communications consumed 184 million kWh of energy procured from the national grid during 
FY 2024-25. Almost 63 million units (~34%) out of 184 million units consumed were produced from 
solar and wind energy. This year, we have added 20.69 million units (‘MU’) of Renewable Energy 
(‘RE’) capacity globally. In India, new RE projects were added with varied RE models, with third-party 
power purchase agreements leading to addition of 1.8 MU, Group captive model leading to 18.8 MU of 
RE addition and Capex based Solar roof top leading to addition of 0.09 MU of RE.
Capital investment on 
energy conservation 
equipmentIn FY 2024-25, 169 projects were completed with a capital investment of ~ H6 crore.
Our Power and Network Infrastructure Services teams identified 169 energy saving opportunities 
involving projects on EB utilisation, electric load reduction, HVAC, PUE Enhancement, Transformer 
and Load Optimisation, SMPS and UPS efficiency enhancement / Optimisation and Consolidation, 
Smart Lighting etc.

ANNEXURE-I
ANNUAL CSR REPORT FOR FY 2024-25
1. A brief outline of the Company’s CSR policy:
 Vision:
‘Creating connected societies to advance the well-
being of people and planet.’
 Recognising the systemic, global challenges of equitable 
resource distribution, social inequality, environmental 
degradation, and climate change, Tata Communications 
envisions a future that prioritises both social and 
planetary well-being. Through a focused strategy, Tata 
Communications’ CSR programmes aim to advance the 
well-being of people and the planet by emphasising 
Sustainable Livelihoods and Environmental conservation 
with Education being a key driver for all. This involves 
skill development, entrepreneurship, protection of water, 
biodiversity, and use of renewable energy sources to 
mitigate carbon emissions. We are working towards 
achieving this through collaboration, partnerships, and 
sustainable practices.
CSR Policy and its alignment with the Tata group 
philosophy:
 CSR at Tata Communications derives inspiration from 
Tata group’s philosophy ‘to improve the quality of life of 
the communities we serve globally through long term 
stakeholder value creation based on leadership with 
trust’ . Tata Communications serves to deliver a New 
World of CommunicationsTM which, can and should 
create social value. We are also committed to making a 
positive, tangible impact on the environment and society. 
Guided by this purpose and Tata group’s philosophy, Tata 
Communications leverages its core expertise, partnerships, 
infrastructure, and other resources to facilitate sustainable 
development and create long term shared value for the 
communities we serve, focused primarily on underserved, 
socially and economically backward groups, including, but 
not limited to, women, children, youth, Dalits & Tribals and 
persons with disabilities.
 Complementing India’s national priorities and policies 
which reflect the spirit of the UN Sustainable Development 
Goals (‘SDGs’), all efforts at Tata Communications are 
aligned to drive action on the following 11 SDGs in 
accordance with our vision and ambition:
	 SDG 1: End poverty in all its forms everywhere.
	 SDG 3: Ensure healthy lives and promote well-
being for all at all ages.
	 SDG 4: Ensure inclusive and equitable quality 
education and promote lifelong learning 
opportunities for all.	 SDG 5: Achieve gender equality and empower all 
women and girls.
	 SDG 7: Ensure access to affordable, reliable, 
sustainable, and modern energy for all.
	 SDG 8: Promote sustained, inclusive, and 
sustainable economic growth, full and productive 
employment, and decent work for all.
	 SDG 10: Reduced Inequality: Reduce inequality 
within and among countries
	 SDG 13: Take urgent action to combat climate 
change and its impacts.
	 SDG 14: Life Below Water: Conserve and sustainably 
use the oceans, seas, and marine resources for 
sustainable development.
	 SDG 15: Life on Land: Protect, restore, and 
promote sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems, 
sustainably manage forests, combat desertification, 
and halt and reverse land degradation and halt 
biodiversity loss
	 SDG 17: Strengthen the means of implementation 
and revitalize the global partnership for 
sustainable development.
 Key focus areas and driving principles:
 Tata Communications is committed to conducting its 
CSR activities in a manner which is rooted in ethics, 
promotes well-being, imparts resilience, and supports 
regeneration. Keeping the community at the centre of 
development while recognising its inter-connectedness 
with natural environment, Tata Communications 
identifies Education, Sustainable Livelihoods and 
Environment as priority areas for its CSR work, 
with health and well-being an integral part to all 
our interventions.
 Implementation of our CSR Programmes:
 The implementation of the CSR programmes approved 
by the Corporate Social Responsibility Safety and 
Sustainability Committee (‘CSRSSC’) and the Board 
in the identified priority areas is done through eligible 
entities / organisations, with an established, impeccable 
track record in their respective domains and the highest 
sense of ethics and integrity.
 The CSRSSC oversees the execution of a selected 
CSR programme including details relating to the time 
period / duration over which the particular programme Tata Communications aims to advance resource-efficient 
urban infrastructure with less greenhouse gas emissions and 
technological solutions for a circular economy by enabling 
our customers in building a more sustainable future together. 
Over the past year we have prioritised sustainability and 
employed technological innovations to address global 
concerns including Climate Change, Gender Equality, Energy 
Conservation, Zero Harm, Human Rights, Water Management 
and Waste Reduction, while also promoting inclusive growth 
for individuals and communities. Our commitment to ‘Zero 
Harm’ applies to our employees, society and the environment.
We have set long-term sustainability targets, to continue our 
efforts towards building a more sustainable organisation and 
future for People, Planet and Communities.
Our sustainability performance can be viewed on our 
website and in the BRSR and the Natural Capital section of 
this Integrated Annual Report.
Human Resources
At Tata Communications, we are committed to creating a 
workplace where every employee feels valued, empowered, 
and inspired to perform at their best.
Our diverse global workforce, spanning multiple continents, 
enriches our culture and fuels continuous technological 
innovation. We promote inclusivity, creating an environment 
where individuals can thrive and grow.
Our HR strategy is anchored in two core principles: 
enhancing employee experience and ensuring strategic 
workforce planning. These are further strengthened by our 
hybrid working model, designed to encourage collaboration 
and synergy across teams.
To learn more about our employee engagement and 
development initiatives, please refer to the Human Capital 
section of this Integrated Annual Report.

 Monitoring and Evaluation:
 In FY 2024-25, Tata Communications collaborated 
with 13 NGO partners for 16 projects across 11 states 
including 14 aspirational districts impacting more than

sustainable impact. Progress on projects is reviewed 
by the CSR team and leadership using a well-defined 
monitoring and evaluation framework with oversight 
from the CSRSSC.
 Monitoring is done, on a quarterly basis by the CSR 
team, through a cloud-based technological tool that 
enables partners to upload real time data along with 
photographs and case studies. The tool facilitates 
last mile tracking and impact analysis. Additionally, 
regular interactions and site visits are conducted by 
the CSR team to assess the progress of the project 
and extend support to the partners. The projects are 
appraised annually by the CSR team, to assess efficacy, 
basis which project engagements are reviewed for the 
consequent year and drawn in the Annual Action Plan 
for the approval of the CSRSSC / Board.

Management Discussion and Analysis Report
MACROECONOMIC & GEOPOLITICAL OVERVIEW
In CY2024, the global economy grew at 3.3%, showing 
resilience amid geopolitical conflicts, trade fluctuations 
and shifting monetary policies. However, the IMF’s World 
Economic Outlook (April 2025) has slightly revised the 
global growth forecast downward to 2.8%, highlighting the 
need for stronger international cooperation.1
This adjustment reflects the impact of trade policy shift, 
particularly renewed tariff measures introduced by the US, 
which have posed significant pressure on global supply 
chain and pricing. Effective policy coordination and prudent 
fiscal management can mitigate these challenges and avert 
deeper disruptions.
The US economy is expected to grow by 1.8% in 2025, 
following a growth of 2.8% in 2024. The growth outlook for 
India is stable at 6.2% in 2025 and 6.3% in 2026, supported 
by private consumption, particularly in rural areas. China’s 
growth outlook stands at 4%, reflecting ongoing adjustments 
and shifts in trade and demand. Meanwhile, other emerging 
markets are navigating tighter financial conditions but 
continue to pursue reforms and partnerships that strengthen 
their economic resilience.
Global disinflation remains underway, with inflation projected 
to ease to 4.3% in 2025 and further to 3.6% in 2026. However, 
inflation expectations for the United Kingdom (‘UK’) have 
been raised from 3.2% to 3.9%, and for the US, from 3.3% 
to 4.3%.2 This upward adjustment reflects persistent pricing 
pressures in the services sector, a recent rebound in core 
goods inflation, and the impact of newly imposed US tariffs. 
Inflation expectations for India are projected to remain stable 
at 4.1% in both 2025 and 2026, indicating a balanced interplay 
between supply-side factors and domestic demand. These 
projections align with the Reserve Bank of India’s medium-
term inflation target, supported by consistent and calibrated 
monetary policy measures. 
However, inflation in emerging and developing Asia, including 
China, is forecast to remain subdued, creating room for 
targeted policy support and sustained domestic demand.
Global trade volumes are expected to grow at a more 
modest pace of 1.7% in 2025. Although trade has been 
impacted by tariff increases and geopolitical developments, 
supply chains are demonstrating adaptability. Ongoing 
diversification efforts, technology adoption, and new trade 
negotiations are helping mitigate the effects of protectionist 
measures and logistical challenges. These developments 
highlight the capacity for adjustment and innovation across 
global markets.In addition to the risks posed by shifting economic policies, 
rising geopolitical tensions are increasingly reshaping the 
global economic outlook. Several key flashpoints are now 
exerting significant influence over macroeconomic dynamics:
US trade policies and related uncertainties
Since early 2025, the United States has implemented 
a series of tariffs to safeguard its domestic economic 
interests, including a 10% blanket tariff on global imports 
and an additional 25% levy on imported vehicles, steel and 
aluminium, effective from April 2025. These measures initially 
triggered uncertainty across global markets, as businesses 
and consumers grappled with potential inflationary pressures 
and employment concerns.
However, on April 9, the US took steps to ease tensions 
by suspending country-specific tariffs for 90 days and 
instituting a uniform 10% tariff for all nations except China. 
This move was followed by more constructive developments, 
including a limited trade agreement with the UK and a 90-
day tariff truce with China, which saw tariffs reduced from 
145% to 30%. Ongoing trade negotiations with India and 
Japan further signal a shift towards greater collaboration and 
equilibrium in global trade dynamics.
The impact on India: 
India was initially impacted by a 26% tariff imposed on April 
2, higher than those on the EU, Japan and South Korea - 
leading to short term market adjustments including a 
temporary dip in the Sensex and value of Rupee. Following 
April 9 policy shift, the overall rate was reduced to 10%, to 
offer some relief.
At a sectoral level: 
	  Pharmaceuticals were spared, providing relief to a 
US$12.2 billion export sector.
	  Automobiles, which constitute 3% of Indian exports to 
the US, now face softer demand and rising costs.
	  IT Services saw the Nifty IT index decline by 3% amid 
recessionary concerns in the US.
	  General exports such as steel, electronics, and gems are 
expected to suffer from reduced price competitiveness.
In response, India is actively pursuing a bilateral trade 
deal with the US, while exporters explore cost-sharing 
mechanisms and market diversification strategies to mitigate 
impact. The broader economic challenges posed by these 
tariffs are being managed through a combination of policy 
diplomacy and private sector resilience.
1. World Economic Outlook, April 2025: A Critical Juncture amid Policy Shifts
2. US Tariffs: What’s the Impact? | J.P. Morgan ResearchTata Communications is closely monitoring these evolving 
dynamics and proactively implementing strategies to 
mitigate associated risks across its global operations.
Russia-Ukraine conflict
Russia continues to face multifaceted geopolitical challenges, 
from the prolonged Ukraine conflict and strained Western 
relations to growing NATO tensions and heavy dependence 
on energy exports. In response, it is deepening alliances with 
China and other BRICS nations, recalibrating its economic 
model, enhancing military capabilities, and working to 
maintain internal stability. As on March 2025, US–Russia 
ceasefire talks on Ukraine may signal a shift in Russia’s 
political and economic trajectory in the months ahead.
Israel-Gaza conflict impacting trade routes in the Red Sea
The Israel–Gaza conflict has had far-reaching effects 
on global trade routes. Houthi-led attacks from Yemen 
have significantly disrupted maritime traffic in the Red 
Sea, leading to: 
	 A 50% drop in Suez Canal traffic
	  An 80-100% rise in transit costs due to rerouting via the 
Cape of Good Hope 
	 Severe damage to telecommunications infrastructure in 
the region
As 2025 unfolds, the global economy remains vulnerable to 
a confluence of risks — from escalating trade disputes and 
protectionism to inflationary pressures and supply chain 
disruptions. These uncertainties highlight the need for 
businesses, investors and policymakers to remain agile and 
vigilant amid ongoing global disruptions.
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
During the year the technology industry has navigated 
multiple headwinds but the industry appears poised for 
growth. According to Gartner, in 2025, more than 80% 
of CIOs plan to invest in foundational capabilities such as 
cybersecurity, Generative AI (‘GenAI’), business intelligence 
and data analytics, and integration technologies like APIs.3  
Similarly, the telecommunications sector is adapting to rising 
global demand, evolving its offerings to meet the needs of 
digitally transforming enterprises. As core telecom services 
become commoditised, constraining pricing power and 
necessitating continued infrastructure investment, operators 
are actively pivoting towards growth. The focus is now on 
leveraging GenAI, shaping the future of 5G/6G, deploying 
emerging technologies strategically, and pursuing growth 
through mergers and acquisitions.
Here are a few key trends that are reshaping the technology 
and telecommunications landscape:	 Surge in Global IT spending
 The global appetite for IT services is set to grow 
significantly in 2025 with organisations scaling tech 
investments to harness AI as a revenue driver. Gartner 
forecasts, global IT spending4 will reach US$5.6 trillion 
in 2025, up 7.5% from 2024. Propelled by GenAI’s rapid 
mainstream adoption, midterm growth expectations have 
been upgraded to a CAGR of 7.9% from 2023 to 2028, with 
total spending expected to reach US$7.4 trillion by 2028.
 Here are the key drivers:
	  As GenAI moves from pilot to production, 
segments like data centre systems, devices and 
software are projected to see double-digit growth 
in 2025, largely due to GenAI hardware upgrade. 
	  By 2026, more than 50% of enterprise 
software spend in application software will be 
influenced by GenAI.
	  Investment will intensify in platforms enabling 
scalable AI deployments — particularly around 
agentic AI with  autonomous gen AI agents that can 
complete complex tasks with minimal human input.
	  Communication services will gain strategic 
importance, especially fixed data services, which 
are projected to grow at a CAGR of 3.2% in five-
years through 20285. High-growth industries 
include communications, media and services, 
power and utilities and healthcare.
	 Cybersecurity: A Strategic Imperative
 With the global cost of cybercrime projected to 
hit US$10.5 trillion6 in 2025, risk management and 
cybersecurity will dominate C-suite priorities. Rising 
threats from IoT, cloud expansion, and GenAI-driven 
sectors are widening the attack surface. In response:
	  The global market for security solutions is expected 
to exceed US$200 billion by 2028.
	  Cybersecurity spending will rise sharply, reinforced 
by geopolitical risks and regulatory mandates.
	  Organisations are enhancing visibility and reporting 
through advanced compliance technology, 
although fragmented data remains a challenge.
	 Cloud Transformation: Toward Hybrid and Multicloud
 The global spend on public cloud services is projected to 
reach US$805 billion in 2024, and is expected to double 
by 2028, driven by scalability, efficiency and AI integration. 
While public cloud has dominated investments, outpacing 
those for private cloud by more than 3:1 in recent years, 
businesses are reassessing the balance between public 
and private cloud, with hybrid and multicloud strategies 
gaining traction to maximise flexibility and control.6

offerings. Their deep expertise in connectivity, edge computing, and AI-enabled network management positions them 
well to drive value in an AI-first world.
	 Investments in Cybersecurity and Data Compliance
 With mounting regulatory scrutiny7, businesses are 
investing heavily in data protection and compliance. 
Executives anticipate rising cybersecurity budgets 
— fuelled by both proactive risk management and 
mandatory compliance requirements. To navigate 
this complex landscape, businesses are adopting 
integrated solutions that improve decision-making, 
reporting, and visibility, while continuing to evolve 
governance frameworks.
	  Increased M&As and partnership activity to gain 
competitive advantage and scale 
 2024 witnessed a wave of transformative tech deals, 
combining strengths in infrastructure, software, 
security, and AI. Beyond traditional M&A, the industry 
is embracing alternative deal structures — such as joint 
ventures and strategic alliances, especially effective 
in times of economic and regulatory uncertainties. 
Partnerships in AI infrastructure, energy-efficient 
software, cybersecurity, and professional services are 
accelerating innovation and unlocking new growth 
opportunities. In 2025, technology and telecom players 
are doubling down on innovation with a sharp focus on 
security, reliability, and trust. As enterprises embrace 
transformation at scale, the industry is redefining itself 
not just as an enabler of digital change, but as a driver 
of long-term sustainable growth.
POLICY DEVELOPMENTS IN INDIA FOSTERING 
GROWTH IN THE ICT INDUSTRY 
Strengthening the Telecom Ecosystem
The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) made 
significant progress in 2024, advancing India’s digital 
ambitions through key initiatives focused on connectivity, 
inclusion, and innovation8. Key developments include:	 The Telecommunications Act, 2023: Replacing colonial-
era legislation, the Indian government introduced the 
Telecommunications Act, 2023, in place of the Indian 
Telegraph Act, 1885 and other laws namely, the Indian 
Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933 and the Telegraph Wires 
(Unlawful Possession) Act, 1950; and also amended the 
Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) Act, 1997. 
The Bill modernises the legal framework governing 
India’s telecom sector. It promotes innovation, 
competition, and secure service delivery, while aligning 
with best global practices. The Act also addresses 
critical issues such as cybersecurity threats, data 
privacy, and regulatory clarity.
	 Accelerated 5G Rollout: India achieved the world’s 
fastest 5G deployment. By March 2024, India had 
4,62,000 5G base stations covering nearly 99% of 
all districts. This rapid rollout is expected to catalyse 
transformation across sectors including healthcare, 
education, manufacturing, and agriculture.
	 Explosive Growth in Internet Access: Internet subscriber 
numbers surged 285%, reaching 969 million by June 
2024. This growth is a major driver of digital inclusion 
and is accelerating socio-economic development across 
urban and rural India.
	 World-Leading Data Affordability: With data costs at 
just US$0.16 per GB, far below the global average of  
US$2.59, India continues to lead in affordable 
connectivity. This has expanded internet access, boosted 
digital literacy and supported inclusive digital growth.
	 Launch of the Sanchar Saathi Portal: The Government 
of India introduced the Sanchar Saathi portal to combat 
telecom-related cybercrime and fraud. The portal, which, 
inter-alia , enables users to trace stolen mobile phones

long-haul fiber connectivity for AI applications. While major tech firms are building their own infrastructure, telcos can 
still offer regional and global connectivity, especially as network capex from tech giants is projected to exceed and  
US$100 billion between 2024 and 2030.
	  Monetising GenAI-Driven Data Growth: GenAI is generating exponential data traffic. While current use cases are 
not bandwidth-intensive, future applications such as AI powered video) could drive significant premium demand for 
ultra-low latency services.
	  Edge Computing Advantage: As smart devices integrate AI chips, demand will shift towards edge computing. Telcos 
are uniquely positioned to deliver on this transition, with real-time data processing closer to the source. Though this 
shift is expected to scale from 2026 onwards, strategic investment now can yield long-term advantage.

	 IndiaAI Mission Boosted with C2,000 crores: Launched 
in April 2024 with an initial budget of C10,400 crores, 
the IndiaAI Mission received an additional C2,000 
crore in funding. This mission focuses on expanding AI 
research, computing capacity, and innovation across 
sectors such as healthcare, agriculture, and governance.
	 Deep Tech Fund of Funds: The Government of India is 
expected to explore the creation of a dedicated Deep 
Tech Fund of Funds to support next-generation start-ups, 
particularly in AI and related fields. It also extended the 
start-up incorporation window by five years, signalling 
long-term commitment to nurturing innovation.
	 MeitY Budget Increased by 48%: The Ministry of 
Electronics and Information Technology (‘MeitY’) has 
been allocated C26,000 crores, an increase by 48% to 
further the IndiaAI mission and support production-
linked incentive schemes for semiconductors, 
electronics, and IT hardware.	 Reduced Import Duties on AI Hardware: To spur 
domestic AI infrastructure, the Budget proposes 
reductions in import duties on AI hardware and 
introduces tax incentives for technology investments, 
helping India remain globally competitive.
	 National Centres of Excellence in Skilling: Five National 
Centres of Excellence for Skilling are to be established 
through global partnerships to advance India’s ‘Make 
for India, Make for the World’ agenda. These centres will 
design industry-aligned curricula, train trainers, and set 
certification standards.
	 Boost to Technological Research: Under the Prime 
Minister’s Research Fellowship scheme, 10,000 
fellowships will be offered over the next five years to 
support advanced research at premier institutions like 
IITs and IISc, with enhanced financial support.
	 Tier-II City Growth for GCC Ecosystem: Expanding 
infrastructure and talent availability in Tier-II cities is a 
priority to strengthen India’s growing Global Capability 
Centre footprint — a key pillar in the country’s digital 
exports strategy.
	 Opening Nuclear Energy to Private Investment: The 
Government plans to amend the Atomic Energy Act, 
1962 to enable private sector participation in nuclear 
energy, aiming to generate at least 100 GW by 2047. 
This is critical for supporting sustainable power 
demands of energy-intensive data centres and future AI 
infrastructure.
These policy and budgetary initiatives reaffirm the 
Government of India’s commitment to building a digitally 
empowered economy. With an emphasis on AI adoption, 
electronics manufacturing, innovation funding, and workforce 
transformation, India is poised to cement its position as a 
global technology leader. The convergence of public policy, 
infrastructure investment, and digital ambition is unlocking 
new pathways for sustainable and inclusive growth.

Integration Challenges Post-Acquisitions
Newly acquired entities and incubation-stage businesses require integration time and investments, which may temporarily 
dilute overall margins despite improving the long-term portfolio strength.
Complex Competitive Landscape: 
The Company faces pressure from multiple fronts: cloud providers expanding into telecom, system integrators offering 
broader managed services, OEMs entering cybersecurity, niche technology vendors directly targeting enterprises and 
traditional telecom players intensifying their focus on business services. This evolving landscape underscores the growing 
importance of strategic collaboration and the delivery of integrated, end-to-end solutions to maintain differentiation and 
market relevance.
Risks from Macroeconomic and Geopolitical Uncertainties
Tata Communications operates in a global environment increasingly shaped by macroeconomic volatility and geopolitical 
tensions. Factors such as infrastructure disruptions, evolving regulatory frameworks, and trade restrictions can impact 
cross-border data flows, network reliability, and enterprise IT spending. Additionally, the Company’s dependence on 
third-party vendors for service delivery introduces further risk—any disruption in their operations can have a direct and 
immediate effect on Tata Communications’ ability to serve its customers.
Evolving Regulatory Landscape
The regulatory environment is becoming increasingly complex, with stricter data sovereignty requirements, cross-border 
compliance obligations, and sector-specific regulations. These evolving mandates demand continuous adaptation and 
sustained investment in robust governance frameworks to ensure compliance, mitigate risks and maintain operational 
resilience across global markets.
